title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme with 2 invertible. For an elliptic curve E/S, the cover J = J_E = (₂E)^* of nonzero 2-torsion points is an étale cover of degree 3; the page calls it a 'cyclic' étale cover. Σ = Σ_J is the P^1-bundle (conic) E/{±1}, which contains the image of J as a relative divisor of degree 3. Σ_J^* is presumably the complement of J in Σ_J. The image of the origin is a section t of Σ_J^*, which plays the role of the Legendre parameter λ.

Conversely, E is recovered as the double cover of Σ branched along the degree-4 divisor J + t. Fix the data (J, t). A double cover branched along J + t is the same as a square root of O_Σ(J+t). Up to pull-back from S, this reduces to the following data:
- an invertible O_S-module T;
- an isomorphism (54) T^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}, where T_{Σ,t} is a canonical invertible module on S built from (Σ, J, t).

The category of such pairs (T, iso) is a μ_2-gerbe over S, namely the gerbe of square roots. Once one object T_0 exists, the gerbe is neutralised. Its category is then equivalent to the category of μ_2-torsors, via (55) E ↦ T_0 ∧^{μ_2} E. This is the familiar quadratic-twist ambiguity: elliptic curves with given (J, t) are torsors for quadratic twisting.

Grothendieck next tries a canonical choice (56) T_0 = O_Σ(1)(t)^♮ = O_Σ(1)(t) ∧^{μ_4} Q_{0S}. Here Q_{0S} is apparently a canonical μ_4-torsor, used to 'twist down' the fibre at t of O_Σ(1). He computes T_0^{⊗2} ≅ O_Σ(2)(t) ∧^{μ_2} μ_4^* ≅ T_{Σ,t} ∧^{μ_2} (μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J). Here μ_4^* (μ_4^♮) is the μ_2-torsor of primitive 4th roots of unity, and ω_J a μ_2-torsor attached to J.

So the canonical candidate squares to the target only up to the μ_2-torsor μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J. A 'reasonable' isomorphism T_0^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t} requires a trivialisation α: μ_4^♮ ≅ ω_J, i.e. a section of μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J. He remarks that α is one of the auxiliary data entering Legendre épinglages.

The next page completes the picture:
- α gives an isomorphism κ_α and hence a canonical 'universal' curve E_α with a Legendre épi-structure subordinate to α.
- For any E with the same (J, t), these structures form a μ_2-torsor L_α(E).
- One has (57) Isom_{S,J}(E_α, E) ≅ L_α(E).

Purpose: to describe the moduli stack of elliptic curves with (twisted) level-2 / Legendre data as a μ_2-gerbe over the λ-line (or its twisted form Σ_J^*), and to neutralise the gerbe by rigidification data (α, or ω). This is a twisted, base-free version of the Legendre family y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ).
errors: The equation labelled '(5)' is almost certainly (54), since the following equations are numbered (55) and (56).

The page's reading of μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J and the exact meaning of Q_{0S} and ω_J depend on earlier pages; no mathematical error is visible, but the identification O_Σ(2)(t) ∧^{μ_2} μ_4^* ≅ T_{Σ,t} ∧ (μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J) is stated without proof here.

ideas.what: Elliptic curve with given 2-torsion cover J and branch section t is equivalent to a square root (T, T^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}) of a line bundle on S, i.e. a double cover of the conic Σ_J branched along J + t
ideas.modern_name: Elliptic curves as double covers of P^1-bundles branched in 4 points; root stacks / gerbe of square roots
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre form); stacky formulation folklore (e.g. Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur era)

ideas.what: Category of square roots is a μ_2-gerbe, neutralised by any object T_0, giving an equivalence with μ_2-torsors via E ↦ T_0 ∧^{μ_2} E
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe of square roots / Kummer gerbe; quadratic twists

ideas.what: The obstruction to a canonical Legendre normalisation is the μ_2-torsor μ_4^* ∧ ω_J (primitive 4th roots of unity twisted by a torsor attached to J); its trivialisation α gives a canonical curve E_α and identifies Isom(E_α, E) with a μ_2-torsor of Legendre structures
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of the μ_2-gerbe M(2) → λ-line; the Legendre family as a section; dependence on a choice of √-1 in twisted settings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; the stack Y(2) ≅ (P^1 − {0,1,∞}) × Bμ_2 is standard

missed.claim: A careful, base-independent (twisted) treatment of Legendre/Jacobi normal forms over arbitrary S with 2 invertible. Non-split 2-torsion cover J and non-trivial μ_4 are allowed, and the exact μ_2-torsor obstruction μ_4^* ∧ ω_J is isolated. This is a refinement of the standard 'Legendre family is a section of the trivial gerbe' statement, which assumes split 2-torsion and usually ignores the role of √-1.
missed.quote: il faut se donner une iso α : μ_4^♮ ≃ ω_J i.e. une section de μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mild interest for arithmetic descent of normal forms over non-closed fields or over Z[1/2]. The content is likely known to specialists in modular stacks but rarely written in this twisted form.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is a careful but essentially standard gerbe-theoretic analysis of quadratic twists and the Legendre normal form. The twisted μ_4/ω_J bookkeeping is a nice unpublished detail but not a new result.

'Quand on a disposé déjà' reads 'Quand on dispose déjà' (or 'Quand on a déjà disposé').
'dans la catégorie des T sur S munis de (5) équivaut' should read 'la catégorie des T sur S munis de (54) équivaut'.
In the iso T_0^{⊗2}: the line shows 'O_Σ(2)(t) ∧_{μ_2} μ_4^*', consistent with the transcription.

The final parenthesis is uncertain. It reads roughly '(ce qui est une des données ... pour une courbe elliptique ... épinglages de Legendre d'une courbe elliptique correspondant à J ...)'. The '15' is likely part of a word, e.g. 'les' or 'ses', not a number.
